summary: On main aa09d05dc (first long run after the f5329feb1 lock-identity fix) the B&W2 demo ran 10000 s with 0 failed render commands and no raster latch. The 'Click on the Gold Scroll' objective appeared between ~8400 s and 9088 s (frames/w125325.png). Aiming used the game's own cursor [0x1d733e8+0xc4/+0xc8] (~0.93 cursor px per relmousemove unit on both axes). Five left clicks at cursor (470,293)/(472,281), where the tooltip read 'Starving villagers', did not consume the scroll (frames/aim2, c1, c3, d0, d1, e1). The sixth, at (495,284) where the game drew its mouse-button hint icon (frames/aim1, f0), consumed it: the scroll box is gone in f1, the gold beam in f2, the objective box in g1 (Field panel 'Food in Field 660'), and g3-g5/final-10000 show the scripted pan to the storehouse and field. Hit counters (click*.out) show every press reached the consumer 0x60ed90 (bit 1 seen at 0x60edad). The dispatcher path 0x611fa0 -> 0x611830(binding 1) returns 0 by design (binding 1 has no case; 0x611efd is the shared return-0 epilogue), and the press is actually consumed by the binding test 0x64c510 -> 0x64c551 (callers 0x64e190/0x64e2a0 -> hand-controller command 0x661fb0). Not reached: free play and an isolated drag attribution (the budget ended ~600 s after the scroll; on Oct 11 free play came ~2000 s after it). Frame rate is lower than on bb9c496ed: 0.090 fps / 629 draws per present in the fixed-view Town Center scene 8101-9080 s, 0.092 fps with the objective up, ~51-67 draws/s versus ~83-95 before. The render worker is saturated (105 min of CPU in 116 min of wall time). The cause is unmeasured; confounders are Node v20 vs v24, a different host, and possible real lock contention since f5329feb1.
